title: Can one picture be added up in more than one way?
description: A picture has a top row of four threes, two rows each with r and s, and a bottom row of four threes. The numbers are added row wise, by like terms, and by doubling the upper half, and all three give the same simplified expression. Keeko's doubt is that the total is twenty four plus r plus s.
teaching_notes: One idea: different ways of adding the same picture simplify to the same expression, two r plus two s plus twenty four. Watch for students who count the r and the s only once although they appear in two rows.

source: A picture has a top row of four 3s, then two rows each with
video_script.why: A learner sees that different ways of adding one picture give the same simplified expression.
video_script.substitution: the book's picture with a top row of four threes, two rows with r and s, and a bottom row of four threes, checked with r as one and s as two
video_script.anchor: the picture of the book: a row of four threes, two rows of r and s, and a row of four threes
video_script.wrong_answer: twenty four plus r plus s
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the r and the s only once although each appears in two rows. Every number in the picture is added, so the idea is broken with r as one and s as two.
video_script.payoff_line: All three ways give two r plus two s plus twenty four

final_answer.spoken: two r plus two s plus twenty four

maths_rules: upper half doubled: 2 x (4 x 3 + r + s) = 2 x (12 + r + s) = 24 + 2r + 2s
Keeko test with r = 1, s = 2: 24 + 1 + 2 = 27, which is not 30
video_script.design: The picture stays on the board; it is added row wise, by like terms and by doubling the upper half, and the three results are simplified to one expression.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a picture with a row 3 3 3 3, two rows r s, and a row 3 3 3 3

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the picture is drawn
marks.top: the top row of four threes is lit
marks.mid: the two rows of r and s are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a picture of numbers.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top row has four threes, and the bottom row has four threes.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Between them are two rows, each with an r and an s.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book wants the sum in three ways. Will three ways give three different answers?

beats.on_screen: the picture stays on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: r and s are unknown numbers; the picture is added in any order

marks.unknown: r and s are shown as covered numbers
marks.order: arrows show the numbers being added in different orders
marks.same: all the arrows end at one total

narration: <bookmark mark='unknown'/>The letter-numbers r and s stand for numbers we do not know.
<bookmark mark='order'/>Numbers can be added in any order.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Whichever way we choose, the total of the picture does not change.

beats.on_screen: Given: rows 3 3 3 3; r s; r s; 3 3 3 3
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a row of four threes, two rows of r and s, and a row of four threes.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum in three ways, simplified

marks.find: the words sum in three ways are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to add all the numbers in three ways, and simplify each.

marks.rows: the four rows are added one after another
marks.long: 12 + r + s + r + s + 12 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step one, add row wise. The rows give four times three, then r plus s twice, then four times three.
<bookmark mark='long'/>That is twelve plus r plus s plus r plus s plus twelve.
<bookmark mark='short'/>The numbers make twenty four, and the letters make two r and two s.

marks.group: all eight threes, both r's and both s's are circled in three colours

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Step two, add like terms together. There are eight threes, two r's and two s's.
<bookmark mark='line'/>That is eight times three, plus two r, plus two s. Again it is twenty four plus two r plus two s.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, upper half doubled: 2 × (4 × 3 + r + s) = 2 × (12 + r + s) = 24 + 2r + 2s

marks.half: the upper half of the picture is lit
marks.twice: the sum of the upper half is written inside a bracket and doubled

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step three, add the upper half and double it, because the lower half matches it.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>The upper half is twelve plus r plus s.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Two times that gives twenty four plus two r plus two s.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Step four, check with r as one and s as two.
<bookmark mark='short'/>The rows add to thirty. Two plus four plus twenty four is also thirty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>All three ways give two r plus two s plus twenty four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the picture
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 24 + r + s, struck out; the test r = 1, s = 2 gives 30 and 27

marks.gap: 30 and 27 appear side by side and do not match
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 2r + 2s + 24 stays

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the total is twenty four plus r plus s. Keeko counted the r and the s once.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try r as one and s as two.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The rows add to thirty, but that idea gives only twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The r and the s each appear in two rows, so each is added twice.
